title: Reading compound words two small words at a time

explain.say: Here is a fun secret. Some long words are two small words stuck together, like building bricks. Look at sunflower on the board. Can you see the two words hiding inside?

draw.text: Reading compound words two small words at a time

explain.say: Look at the first part glowing: sun. You know that word! The bright thing in the sky. Point up and say sun.
Now the second part: flower. Put them together: sun, flower, sunflower! A big yellow flower that looks like the sun. Can you read it?
Here is another one: football. Foot plus ball. Kick your foot and say it! Words made of two words are called compound words. Can you find the two words in football?
And rainbow: rain plus bow. Wonderful! When a long word looks big, hunt for a small word inside. Challenge: what two words make toothbrush?

faq.a: A compound word is two words joined to make one new word, like sun and flower making sunflower.

faq.q: How do I read a compound word?
faq.a: Cover the second half with your finger and read the first word. Then read the second word and push them together.
Football, rainbow, toothbrush, bedroom, cupcake and sunflower are all compound words.

faq.q: Do the two words tell me the meaning?
faq.a: Often they do. A toothbrush is a brush for teeth. A bedroom is a room with a bed. Thinking about both words helps you understand.
asks: What does a compound word mean?

faq.q: How can I practise compound words?
faq.a: Write small words on cards, like sun, flower, foot and ball, and join them to make big words. A teacher or grown-up can play a matching game with you.

facts: Sunflower, football and rainbow are compound words.
A compound word joins two words to make one new word.

quiz.why: Tooth plus brush makes toothbrush: a brush for your teeth.

wrong.1: The first word is tooth, not to.
wrong.2: Look again: it is tooth, not teeth, and brush, not bush.

quiz.say: Which word is a compound word?

wrong.1: Happy does not split into two real words.
